quotes.text: Finance teams don't lack information. They have plenty. The friction is in how you access it and act on it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the real problem Copilot addresses in finance in one sharp line.

quotes.text: Co-pilot amplifies good processes and bad ones equally. If your collections workflow is a mess, Co-pilot won't fix it. It'll just help you generate messy emails faster.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable warning to fix processes before rolling out AI.

quotes.text: Co-pilot doesn't replace finance professionals. It doesn't make journal entries on its own. It doesn't approve payments. What it does is automate the mechanical parts.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly sets expectations about the role of Copilot versus human judgment.

quotes.text: Co-pilot respects your existing security roles. It only shows what that user already has permission to see.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Answers a common security concern in plain language.

quotes.text: Finance teams have always been good at answering one question. What happened? Co-pilot helps them move to a better one. What should we do about it?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the shift from reactive reporting to proactive decisions.

chapters.title: Introduction and the problem Copilot solves

takeaways: Copilot in Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations brings customer summaries, draft emails, variance explanations and forecasts into the finance workflow instead of making people chase data across screens.
Collections is the fastest-value starting point, followed by financial close, cash flow forecasting and expense and AP automation.
Copilot requires a recent F&O version, Dataverse integration, a cloud-hosted environment and a separate Microsoft 365 Copilot license, and adoption needs targeted pilots and scenario-based training.
hook: Most finance teams hear Copilot and picture a chatbot, but what does it really do on a Tuesday morning? This episode walks finance professionals and Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations users through collections, month-end close, cash flow forecasting and AP, plus the requirements and adoption steps that decide whether it pays off.
